core_obligations: Parts (1) and (2) (proof lines 348-351): the algebra is a nonzero module over itself, so the first assertion follows from the second; for the second, a submodule of minimal finite dimension over the ground field is simple, and such a submodule exists because a cyclic submodule is finite dimensional.

Part (3) (proof lines 352-353): for a simple module and a nonzero element, the submodule generated by the element times the algebra is a nonzero submodule and hence the whole module, which gives finite dimensionality.
Part (4) (proof lines 353-354): a nonzero endomorphism of a simple module has zero kernel and therefore is an isomorphism, so the endomorphism ring is a skew field.
proof_roadmap: Get the existence of a simple module from a minimal dimensional submodule.
Use cyclicity to exhibit a finite dimensional submodule.
Transport simplicity to the two remaining statements.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects basic facts about modules over a finite algebra: there is a simple module, every nonzero module has a simple submodule, a simple module is finite dimensional, and the endomorphism ring of a simple module is a skew field (statement lines 336-346). The proof is a complete argument: the first assertion follows from the second because the algebra is a nonzero module over itself, and the second holds by taking a submodule of minimal finite dimension, whose existence is guaranteed by cyclicity (proof lines 348-351); finite dimensionality of a simple module follows from the submodule generated by an element (proof lines 352-353); and a nonzero endomorphism of a simple module is injective and hence an isomorphism, which makes its endomorphism ring a skew field (proof lines 353-354). The non-formal content is the minimal dimensional submodule argument. The claim is H2.
